Milan Monumental Cemetery- the Jewish Section

Cemetery · Milan, Italy

The Jewish Section was inaugurated in 1872, and replaced the previous Jewish Cemetery as a replacement for the previous Fopponino burial complex. The Section was part of the overall plan of the Monumental Cemetery designed by architect Carlo Maciachini, in 1863. The monument to the Jewish Martyrs of the Nazis stands to the right of the main entrance, unveiled in 1947 and designed by architect Manfredo d’Urbino bearing the names of twelve victims of the Holocaust who died in different circumstances, positioned around a large marble menorah. The central building that originally marked the entrance and then became a funeral chamber was restored and enriched with polychrome stained glass panes designed by the artist Diego Penacchio Ardemagni in 2014, who drew inspiration from Marc Chagall’s at the Hadassah Hospital in Jerusalem.
